reason: Verified by driving the master and reading b.css and render-b.js. Every measurement holds: state=day renders .b-dayToday at 12px Geist Mono 400 uppercase, .b-dayNames at 48px Geist 600, .b-dayDate 20px, .b-dayNowTitle 24px; state=phone renders .b-num at 96px mono; owner-flight and desk render it at 148px. The like-for-like comparison is phone 96 against day 48, since MEDIUM in render-b.js maps day to 'phone' -- the finding's desk/day pairing is loose, but its own numbers are all correct and the halving on the same medium is real. The finding survives the note's two tests. First, the word: the lock reserves 96 and 148 for 'the count, which is the whole composition', and b.css:640 and render-b.js:695 both say the count is a countdown and an arrived countdown is a word, so 'Today' IS the count in its resolved form. A word taking the number's place should take the number's slot; the build instead moves it into the 12px mono micro-label register and hands the display register to the couple's names, which are 11px mono (.b-who) on every other state. That is a register swap on exactly one state -- the count demoted to a micro-label, a micro-label promoted to display -- which breaks the direction's stated hierarchy ('the count, the date and what the day is are the first three things on the surface, in that order') far more than setting the word at the step breaks the ramp. Setting 'Today' at 96 honours the lock; leaving it at 12 is what strains it. Second, the sans question: the ramp reserves those steps for the count, not for a face, and the author already wrote Geist 600 at 96 for this exact element -- b.css:723, '[data-medium="full"] .b-dayNames { font-size: 96px }' -- which is unreachable dead code because day never leaves phone medium. So a sans word at 96 is already inside the constraint and was already intended for this screen; the constraint objection fails. No palette, weight, family or architecture rule is touched. Not already handled: round 1's 'the-day-itself-is-empty' was refuted on content and its sharpened fix (place line, Happening now, keepsake list) was built -- none of it touched scale. The fix as written needs three corrections, hence the sharpened version.
sharpenedFix: Restore the count register on state=day; do not relocate the composition. (1) Set the resolved count at the 96 step inside .b-dayWrap, keeping that block's centred axis. The fix's 'in the exact position the number occupies on every other state' would move it to the horizon's left-aligned column and trade a scale defect for a layout one -- the arrival card is deliberately centred and should stay centred. (2) Face: sans at 96 is permitted (b.css:723 already writes it), but the count's material identity is Geist Mono 400 with --track-display and the -0.05em optical bearing that b.css:60 exists to fix; setting 'Today' in that same mono keeps the arrived count reading as the same object rather than a different one. Measured at 390: 'Today' is 274px in mono 400 at 96 and 257px in Geist 600 at 96, against a 300px .b-dayWrap column -- mono clears by 26px, so fit-test at 320-360 device widths and, if it does not clear, drop to the 64 step rather than switch family. (3) Drop the proposed mono unit reading the weekday: .b-dayDate already states 'Saturday 3 October 2026' and the unit would repeat it -- 'days' was the thing being counted and there is nothing left to count, so the unit slot resolves to nothing. (4) The fix is factually wrong that 20 is 'where MARA & FINN already sits on every other surface': .b-who is 11px Geist Mono 400 uppercase everywhere else. Demote .b-dayNames to that exact .b-who register so the day screen is recognisably the same composition arriving; 20 is defensible only as a fresh choice for the arrival card, not as a restoration. (5) '148 at desk width' is unreachable as written -- MEDIUM in render-b.js maps day to 'phone', so the state never renders at full/sheet. Either scope this to phone only and delete the dead rule at b.css:723, or change the medium map, which is a separate decision and not part of this finding. (6) Lifting 'Wedding day' 24 to 30 is in the ramp and harmless but incidental; the register inversion is the finding and is where the effort belongs.
